Article 60 - Document Retention

Operators of rubber processing factories must retain documents concerning the receipt and dispatch of all rubber in a systematic manner and readily accessible, for example: production and processing records, production and processing data, sales and distribution documents, certificates of origin or export permits, reports and other related documents.

Document retention must ensure security and be preserved for at least ten years, including both original and duplicate copies in both conventional systems and electronic systems.

Measures for System Recovery

Article 96 Measures for System Recovery
Measures for system recovery are as follows:
1. Response to emergency incidents;
2. Backup and system recovery;
3. Other measures deemed necessary.

Article 37 Response to Emergency Incidents
Legal persons and organizations must establish procedures and methods for responding to emergency incidents in order to assess, control and limit cybersecurity threats in a timely manner and then report to the specialized committee and the Ministry of Technology and Communications.

Article 38 Backup and Data Recovery
Legal persons and organizations must back up data in cloud systems and/or hardware, including multiple backups, so as to be able to recover the backed-up data in the event of an emergency incident.

Article 18 - Consideration of Designation to the Domestic List

The Ministry of Public Security shall consider proposals for designation to the domestic list on the basis of the following grounds:

1. A natural person, legal person, organization or group of persons, if there is substantive and sufficient evidence that can prove or confirm that such natural person, legal person, organization or group of persons has the purpose of providing assistance, support, funding, equipment or technology, goods or services, or conduct or activities as defined in the Law on Counter-Terrorism, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism and related laws and regulations.

2. A natural person, legal person, organization or group of persons that a foreign state requests to be designated to the domestic list, whereby the requesting state has substantive and sufficient evidence that can confirm that such person has conduct or activities as defined in the Law on Counter-Terrorism, Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism and related laws and regulations.

Following consideration by the Ministry of Public Security and finding that there is substantive and sufficient evidence that can confirm that the conduct or activities of a natural person, legal person, organization or group of persons meets the grounds as specified in the clauses of this Article, it shall propose to the competent authority to consider designation to the domestic list or submit a request to foreign states immediately through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs without necessity of going through criminal proceedings or having a court judgment and without necessity of a criminal act having occurred.

The Ministry of Public Security shall inform the rights, obligations and details of the request to the natural person, legal person, organization or group of persons that is designated to the domestic list after the competent authority has designated the list.
